brief: make an ad for my vitamin C serum, before and after style

context.audience: women 25-40 who care about skincare and dislike hype

concept: Same morning light, same mirror-free angle, two weeks apart: the glow does the talking.
plan_outline: 1. MCU · eye · static · bathroom window light · a woman's face, natural skin, slightly dull, soft morning light from the left (3 s, before)
2. ECU · eye · static · white marble · one drop falls from the dropper onto the back of a hand (2 s)
3. MCU · eye · static · identical framing and light · the same face, clearer and brighter, a small smile (3 s, after; a match cut)
4. CU · eye · orbit · white marble, soft side light · the bottle with an orange glow through the glass (2 s)
5. End card (page) · logo, 'Two weeks. Your light.' (2 s)
why: Before/after only works with identical framing and light: the change is the only variable, so the viewer believes it.
No mirror (models get reflections wrong) and no exaggerated transformation — honest results build trust.
The drop is the single product moment; the label stays soft so no garbled lettering appears.
Never invent clinical claims; the line is a feeling, not a percentage.
